title: arXiv Mathematics — Friday, 30 October 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart. This inferred ordering uses checkable mathematical results, cross-listing, and sparse external signals; very recent papers have little usable citation history, so this is a notable-recent-papers selection rather than measured popularity.

sections.title: A proof of the Murty--Simon conjecture on diameter-2-critical graphs
sections.abstract: The authors prove the Murty--Simon conjecture for every n-vertex diameter-2-critical graph: it has at most floor(n^2/4) edges, with equality only for the balanced complete bipartite graph.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A precise all-n resolution of a long-standing extremal graph conjecture, including the equality case; the authors contrast this with the earlier result for sufficiently large n only.
sections.claimed_result: The authors' Theorem 1.1 proves the floor(n^2/4) edge bound for every n>=3 and identifies the unique equality graph.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite simple graphs on n>=3 vertices that have diameter 2 and lose that property after deletion of any edge.
sections.unique_caveat: The manuscript says AI found the initial proof of the edge bound; the authors report simplifying it and extending it to prove the full conjecture. This preprint's proof has not been independently verified here.

sections.title: Quantitative sub-ballisticity of self-avoiding walk on Z^d
sections.abstract: For d>=2, the authors give an explicit exponential upper bound on the probability that an n-step self-avoiding walk reaches distance at least vn, yielding a high-probability displacement bound of order n/exp(c log* n).
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It upgrades the cited qualitative sub-ballisticity result to an explicit rate, and its proof-theoretic approach is cross-listed between probability and logic. The authors also derive a quantitative bridge-partition estimate.
sections.claimed_result: The authors bound the probability of linear displacement by exp(-n/T(v)) for explicit T(v) and sufficiently large n, and derive the stated n/exp(c log* n) displacement scale with very high probability.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The uniform law on length-n self-avoiding walks starting at the origin in the hypercubic lattice Z^d, for each fixed d>=2.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper says the precise asymptotic of its improved connective-constant error term is beyond scope; stronger displacement bounds would follow if the bridge partition function had the expected polynomial decay.

sections.title: Nonuniqueness of the 2D Euler Evolutions with L^1 cap L^p Vorticity
sections.abstract: For every prescribed 1<p<infinity, the authors construct compactly supported planar vorticity in L^1 cap L^p that has two distinct exact Lagrangian evolutions under the unforced two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper gives a concrete nonuniqueness construction while retaining strong L^1 cap L^p continuity and exact transport by measure-preserving regular Lagrangian flows.
sections.claimed_result: The authors construct two evolutions from the same datum that remain distinct at a positive time, detected by a fixed smooth observable.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Unforced 2D incompressible Euler on [0,1]; for each finite p>1, the compactly supported initial vorticity and construction parameters may depend on p.
sections.unique_caveat: The construction establishes existence for selected data, not nonuniqueness for every L^1 cap L^p datum. The introduction notes an independently developed manuscript using essentially the same core mechanism.

sections.title: A Sharp Uniqueness-Nonuniqueness Dichotomy for Neutral Vortex Arrays in 2D Euler Equations
sections.abstract: For stationary arrays of disjoint neutral vortices, the authors give a sharp integral criterion in terms of an envelope of vorticity L^p norms that separates uniqueness from nonuniqueness.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a two-way criterion for every finite nondecreasing envelope, rather than only an example or one-sided sufficient condition; it is a companion result to the same team's Euler construction above.
sections.claimed_result: If I_Theta=integral Theta(p)^-1 dp diverges, every array in the specified class has a unique evolution, even among bounded energy-admissible weak velocity solutions; if it converges, an array with two distinct unforced Lagrangian Euler evolutions exists.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The criterion is within a class of stationary arrays of disjoint neutral vortices and an arbitrary finite, nondecreasing envelope Theta for vorticity L^p norms.
sections.unique_caveat: The sharp dichotomy is not claimed for arbitrary initial vorticities or all Euler solution classes; its stated scope is the neutral-array class.

sections.title: The Kawatani--Okawa conjecture in dimensions three and four
sections.abstract: The authors prove that a smooth projective threefold or fourfold whose bounded derived category has no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition has nef canonical divisor, confirming the Kawatani--Okawa conjecture in those dimensions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A clearly scoped conjecture result in two dimensions, supported by a stated combination of extremal-contraction classification and admissible-subcategory constructions.
sections.claimed_result: For smooth projective threefolds and fourfolds under the no-nontrivial-semiorthogonal-decomposition hypothesis, the canonical divisor is nef.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth projective varieties of dimension 3 or 4; the hypothesis concerns the bounded derived category.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is limited to dimensions three and four; it does not establish the corresponding statement in higher dimensions.

sections.title: JT gravity as a conformal scaling limit of random flat combinatorial disks
sections.abstract: The authors prove that a Boltzmann ensemble of random rectilinear combinatorial disks, with a distinguished side length tending to infinity, converges after rescaling to a continuum random surface described by flat Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A precise conformal scaling-limit theorem bridges discrete random geometry, probability, and mathematical physics; an independent secondary write-up also appeared shortly after the preprint.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish convergence of the rescaled conformal factors on compact interior subsets and give a branching-exploration criterion for analogous discrete models.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The proved example is the Boltzmann ensemble of rectilinear disks; the criterion requires a Markov exploration, tightness, and convergence of the relevant length process and associated data.
sections.unique_caveat: The extension to other natural models, such as flat triangulations or quadrangulations, is presented as an expectation and route for future work, not as a proved universality theorem.

sections.title: Convergence of a drainage network model with branching to the Brownian net
sections.abstract: For a branching version of a long-range-dependent drainage network, the authors prove that its scaling limit is the Brownian net, resolving a conjecture for this model and examining a broader range of scaling regimes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors explicitly identify the Brownian-net limit as a conjecture from prior work and state that they prove it; the paper also appeared in an external probability-paper listing.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove convergence to the Brownian net for the stated branching drainage-network model and extend the scaling-regime analysis beyond the earlier treatment.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Coalescing random walks with long-range dependence before coalescence, with branching probabilities that are small and vary with the scaling parameter.
sections.unique_caveat: This resolves the limit question for the model and regimes treated; it does not classify scaling limits for arbitrary drainage networks or branching rules.

sections.title: Global Well-Posedness of Landau Equation in Bounded Domains
sections.abstract: The authors prove global well-posedness near a Maxwellian for the Landau equation in bounded C^3 domains with in-flow or diffuse-reflection boundary conditions, covering -3<=gamma<=1 including Coulomb interactions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The stated global strong-solution result covers the full listed interaction range, including Coulomb, while treating bounded domains and two specified boundary conditions; it is a substantial theorem-level PDE signal.
sections.claimed_result: Small compatible Gaussian perturbations generate global strong solutions, with uniqueness and continuous dependence among weak solutions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Initial data are small compatible Gaussian perturbations of a Maxwellian; the domain is bounded and C^3, with in-flow or diffuse-reflection boundaries.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a near-equilibrium theorem under compatibility and boundary regularity assumptions, not a large-data global result.

sections.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperkähler Manifolds
sections.abstract: The authors show that every compact hyperkähler manifold is bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojević and Stelzig, deriving the result from algebraic formality theorems for multicomplexes and commutative n-differential graded algebras.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper combines a universal statement for compact hyperkähler manifolds with an explicit algebraic framework and is cross-listed across algebraic topology, algebraic geometry, and differential geometry.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish a model-category structure for the relevant multicomplexes, generalize the partial-bar-partial lemma, and prove an algebraic formality theorem that yields strong formality for compact hyperkähler manifolds.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compact hyperkähler manifolds and the pluripotential homotopy theory / multicomplex setting specified by the authors.
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusion is the stated bigraded strong-formality property; it should not be read as a claim about arbitrary compact complex manifolds.
